title: Dev flow v2 adjudication record — one round's batch
$comment: Orchestrator-authored, NOT wrapped in result.envelope.schema.json — the envelope is for agent->orchestrator results (see specs/dev-flow-v2.md 'Roles and authority' table); the orchestrator writes this document and run.schema.json directly. One instance covers one round's worth of NEW adjudications, matching how evidence is posted (docs/decisions/0002: 'one comment per round, the moment the round is adjudicated'). The property this family holds a finding to is: exactly one adjudication per finding, per run, ever — enforced in three parts, each by a different mechanism, because no single one of them can see the whole run: (1) within ONE document, the finding_id pattern plus scripts/validate-result-schemas.mjs's checkAdjudicationEntries reject a duplicate finding_id in the same adjudications[] array; (2) a finding_id's own <stage>-r<round> segments must equal THIS document's stage/round (checkAdjudicationIdAttribution, always on, no external context needed — the id grammar makes it local) — this is what stops a finding from one round's document from being silently re-adjudicated under a different round's stage/round claim; (3) across EARLIER round documents of the same run, --known-adjudicated (a JSON array of finding ids already adjudicated by those documents) rejects any entry naming one of them. A run's full adjudicated view is the union of every round's adjudication document for that run. `settlements[]` is deliberately NOT here: specs/dev-flow-v2.md states the run record is 'the only home of mutable run state' and settlements are appended over time as `defer` dispositions resolve during integration, so they live in run.schema.json instead — see its own $comment and ai/schemas/README.md 'Where settlements live'.

stage.description: challenge/review: adjudicates a reviewer pass's findings (--pass names a reviewer envelope). integration: adjudicates an integrator payload's findings instead (--pass names an integrator envelope) — its findings carry no reviewer-asserted priority, so the validator's pass cross-check skips the reviewer_priority fidelity comparison for this stage (ai/schemas/README.md).

reviewed_head.description: The head this round's pass(es) reviewed — must equal every adjudicated finding's originating pass's reviewed_head. Checked by the validator's run-context mode, which has the pass documents in hand.

adjudications.description: Every finding introduced by this round, each adjudicated exactly once (docs/product/domain.md: 'A finding is adjudicated exactly once, and its adjudication is the only view scripts read'). 'Keyed by finding id' (specs/dev-flow-v2.md) is realized here as an array of entries each carrying its own finding_id, with uniqueness enforced by the validator — the hand-rolled subset validator has no patternProperties or schema-valued additionalProperties, so a JSON object dynamically keyed by finding id is not expressible; an array of tagged objects is the same shape already used for findings[]/checks[]/ac_test_map[] throughout this schema family.

reviewer_priority.description: A copy of the finding's own reviewer-asserted priority, carried here so reviewer-vs-orchestrator disagreement is measurable from this document alone, without re-reading the pass (specs/dev-flow-v2.md: 'the raw reviewer output is kept so reviewer-vs-orchestrator disagreement can be measured'). The validator's run-context mode still cross-checks it against the originating pass's finding.

reason.description: Why this disposition, always required — every adjudication explains itself, not only overrides.

override.description: null when adjudicated_priority equals reviewer_priority. Required (a non-null object with a reason) whenever they differ — specs/dev-flow-v2.md's upward-override / disagreement record. This is a cross-field (not cross-document) condition — adjudicated_priority and reviewer_priority are two sibling values within ONE entry — but the subset validator's if/then cannot express 'these two properties are unequal' (JSON Schema has no field-to-field comparison operator), so it is enforced as a semantic check, not a structural keyword. See ai/schemas/README.md.
